title: Ops prioritization scratchpad — PM↔Eng 1:1 (Rhea)
body:
Meeting goal: quick sync with Eng Lead to unblock feature prioritization for next sprint, align on risk/mitigation for Dedicated rollout, and confirm observable signals for the Console latency incident runbook.

Context / one-line summary:
- Product is prioritizing API+Console improvements to hit latency SLOs for short requests (<=128 tokens) while avoiding cost regression for long-tail Dedicated workloads.
- Recent Dedicated cluster saturation during peak hours exposed a fallback routing bug; want a plan for safe rollouts and a short-term mitigation.

Agenda (30 min):
1) 5m — Quick status: Dedicated capacity shortfall + incident postmortem highlights (who owns followups)
2) 10m — Prioritization tradeoffs: small-surface API optimizations (prefix cache) vs Console UX perf (streaming changes)
3) 8m — Rollout plan for new routing policy + canary strategy for Private deployments
4) 5m — Action items, owners, and dates

Talking points / notes to self: 
- Incident summary: 2025-02-10 peak spike; autoscaler failed to trigger on one AZ (INF-3421). Worst-case latency increased x4 for 30 minutes. Root cause: mis-evaluated metric (worker_utilization_v2) and a routing fallback that accidentally sent requests to CPU-only nodes.
- Immediate ask: validate a short patch to avoid CPU-only fallback for golden-tier customers until autoscaler fix ships. Patch = runtime check + config flag. Ask Marcus to assign eng owner and estimate (target: <=48h).

Decision topics (need yes/no or relative priority):
- Q1: Do we prioritize prefix/KV-cache changes that give ~15–25% p50 improvement for short prompts but require a rolling restart? Tradeoffs: restart causes transient capacity dip.
  - My leaning: defer restarts for next non-peak window unless we can do a staged rollout to a subset of regions.
- Q2: Console streaming change (switch to chunked responses with backpressure hints) — customer-facing but lower impact on overall unit cost. Do we ship beta behind flag?
  - Leaning: ship behind feature flag to 10% of orgs using Console for interactive demos.
- Q3: Private deploys — do we require a separate preflight that validates all routing policy variants (local + remote fallbacks) before certifying?
  - Proposal: yes, add a lightweight preflight smoke test; small maintenance cost but prevents the last incident class.

Metrics / signals to review in the meeting:
- p50/p95 token latency for <=128 tokens, by model and region (last 7d) — show whether prefix cache would move p95 significantly.
- Node utilization distribution and autoscaler trigger histograms during peak.
- Errors from 'fallback-to-cpu' metric and number of requests affected (split by customer tier).

Risks / mitigations: 
- Rolling restart risk: capacity dip. Mitigation: staged canary by region, reserving burst capacity in Dedicated for the window (use reserved pool).
- Private rollout variance: customers may have different overlay networks causing routing flakiness. Mitigation: require preflight plus a 'soft-rollout' where we keep the old policy live for 15 minutes and monitor.
- Console change: could increase client-side CPU for streaming reassembly. Mitigation: add client-side telemetry opt-in for beta.

Concrete asks for Marcus (Engineering Lead):
- Assign eng owner for CPU-fallback patch and schedule ETA (48–72h).
- Approve staged restart plan and confirm if SRE can temporarily bump Dedicated reserved pool for a 2-hour window next week.
- Quick review of preflight test checklist for Private deploys (I drafted a checklist in Confluence link above).

Draft action items (owner — due):
- Patch to block CPU-only fallback for golden tier — Marcus / eng-oncall (owner TBD) — due 2025-02-16
- Prepare staged restart runbook and request reserved pool bump — SRE (Noah) — due 2025-02-18
- Feature-flag toggles for Console streaming beta + telemetry opt-in — Platform SDK team (Elena) — due 2025-02-21
- Add preflight smoke test to Private deploy pipeline (small shell script + routing checklist) — Marcus / infra eng — due 2025-02-20
- Update runbook and dashboard to expose 'fallback-to-cpu' broken-out by customer tier — Observability (Marcus + Ops) — due 2025-02-19

Prep notes / quick references to drop in the meeting:
- Link to PR with the autoscaler fix branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/897
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INF-3421 (postmortem draft attached to Confluence page)
- Quick query snippets to run during sync:
  - "SELECT percentile(latency_ms, 50), percentile(latency_ms,95) FROM token_latency WHERE tokens <= 128 AND region='us-west-2'"
  - "count(fallback_to_cpu) BY customer_tier WHERE last_24h > 0"

Open questions I want to ask Marcus: 
- Any reason the autoscaler metric change (worker_utilization_v2) was rolled out without a rollback guard? Is this a process gap?
- Are there capacity reservations we can burn for prioritized restarts that don't require red-team approvals?
- If we opt to ship prefix cache change during low-traffic hours, what's a safe per-AZ % exposure for canary? 5%? 10%?

Notes to self post-meeting (placeholders to fill):
- Capture exact owner names and PR links for each action item.
- Schedule follow-up in 3 days to validate CPU-fallback patch in staging and confirm canary window.

Quick personal TODOs before meeting (today):
- Pull p50/p95 charts for last 7 days and export snapshots (Console + API).
- Send 1-line pre-read to Marcus + Noah with the 3 asks and the incident summary.
- Open a short JIRA for the preflight smoke test (link to add in meeting).

Tone notes: keep meeting focused, avoid deep infra design in a 30m slot — aim for owners + dates. If Marcus wants deep design, schedule follow-up with infra + SRE.

-- end scratchpad --
